documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, nice progress. AST 104 and ALT 118, down from 450 and 520 in the ED, and bilirubin is 1.4, nearly normal. One more check in about a month. Keep avoiding alcohol and keep acetaminophen to a minimum. The hepatitis C virus test is still running; I'll send it to hepatology when it's back.

conditions.label: Chronic hepatitis C
conditions.note: Sustained virologic response after sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, 2024-07-08 to 2024-09-29.

documents.title: Hepatology Follow-up
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology group

Dear Doctor,
Ms. Lambert completed 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir on 09/29/2024 without missed doses. HCV RNA was not detected in the emergency department on 12/20/2024 and again on 01/21/2025, 16 weeks after the last dose. This is a sustained virologic response: her hepatitis C is cured.

We note the isoniazid liver injury in December, recovering on your 01/21 panel (AST 104, ALT 118, bilirubin 1.4); please continue liver tests until it settles. The cryoglobulinemia features are gone: no purpura or joint pain, and creatinine 1.0 with a negative urinalysis in September.

Her HCV antibody will stay positive for life, so any future check should be HCV RNA. With FIB-4 1.41 before treatment, she needs no routine hepatology follow-up; we are glad to see her again for any liver concern. No alcohol.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Sincerely,
Hepatology

conditions.label: Toxic liver disease with acute hepatitis

documents.title: February results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, your liver tests have come most of the way back from the isoniazid: AST 61, ALT 66, bilirubin 1.1, close to where they ran for years. I'm calling the drug injury resolved. Metanephrines normal again this year. Next visit in April for blood pressure; we'll do the physical in the fall.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice
Date of service: 06/23/2025

Yearly oral examination for benign leukoplakia. The mouth soreness settled about 4 weeks into the dexamethasone rinse last summer, and she has not needed it since. Wrists no longer itch. Hepatitis C treated last year and cured.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: both buccal mucosae with the white, net-like plaques, unchanged; no new, thickened, red or ulcerated area. Tongue, floor of mouth and gums normal. Wrists with faint brown marks where the papules were, no active papules.

Assessment: benign oral leukoplakia, stable. Lichen planus, quiet.

Plan: oral examination yearly; sooner for any new, thickening, red or non-healing area.

Dermatology

reports.text: Complete abdominal ultrasound with Doppler. Liver: nodular surface contour and coarse heterogeneous echotexture; no focal lesion. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow; hepatic veins patent. No biliary dilation; gallbladder surgically absent. Spleen enlarged, 15.2 cm. Moderate ascites in all four quadrants. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver morphology with splenomegaly and moderate ascites. Patent portal vein. No focal liver lesion.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Gastroenterology
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, gastroenterology service (MICU 07/02-07/04, then ward)
Admitted 07/02/2025, discharged 07/07/2025

Patient: Julie Lambert, 53

Presentation: several episodes of vomiting bright red blood over 4 hours. For about 6 months, progressive abdominal swelling and fatigue; for the past few months, easy bruising and ankle swelling. Background: hepatitis C since 2011 (incomplete course in 2012; cured with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in 2024) with mixed cryoglobulinemia, isoniazid liver injury in December 2024, resected pheochromocytoma, lichen planus, oral leukoplakia, hypertension. No alcohol since 2018 after more than a decade of daily drinking.

Admission exam: T 37.1 C, BP 94/60, HR 112, RR 20. Pale and fatigued. Scleral icterus. Spider angiomata across the chest. Abdomen distended with a fluid wave; spleen palpable; prominent tortuous veins radiating from the umbilicus. Rectal exam: no blood.

Admission labs: hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, platelets 84,000/mm3, AST 162, ALT 94, alkaline phosphatase 188, total bilirubin 4.3, direct bilirubin 2.1, albumin 2.5, INR 1.7. Renal function normal.

Hospital course:
1. Acute esophageal variceal hemorrhage. Octreotide infusion, IV pantoprazole, ceftriaxone. Urgent upper endoscopy on 07/02: markedly dilated varices in the distal esophagus with stigmata of recent bleeding; 5 bands placed. Stomach and duodenum normal. Octreotide for 72 hours. No further bleeding. Not transfused. Ceftriaxone changed to oral ciprofloxacin to complete 7 days. Discharge hemoglobin 8.9.
2. Cirrhosis due to hepatitis C (virus cured 2024) with portal hypertension and ascites, newly recognized. Ultrasound with Doppler: nodular liver, splenomegaly 15.2 cm, moderate ascites, patent portal vein, no liver mass. Diagnostic paracentesis: ascitic neutrophils 110/mm3, ascitic albumin 0.9 g/dL (SAAG 1.6), culture no growth; no SBP. Diuretics started. No encephalopathy.
3. Hypertension: hydrochlorothiazide stopped given admission hypotension and new diuretics.

Discharge medications:
- Propranolol 20 mg twice daily (new)
- Spironolactone 100 mg daily (new)
- Furosemide 40 mg daily (new)
- Pantoprazole 40 mg daily for 14 days (new)
- Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 2 more days (new)
- STOP hydrochlorothiazide
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: 2 g sodium diet; no alcohol; no NSAIDs; acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day. Weigh daily.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with BMP, CBC, liver panel and INR; repeat upper endoscopy with banding in about 4 weeks (scheduled 07/30).

events.reason: Hospital follow-up, variceal bleed and new cirrhosis

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Admitted 7/2-7/7 with bleeding esophageal varices; banded x5. New diagnosis of cirrhosis from hep C with ascites. Reviewed the discharge summary with her line by line.

She's shaken. Says the belly had been getting bigger since about January and she put it down to weight gain; ankles puffy since spring; bruising easily. No further vomiting of blood, stools brown. Taking propranolol 20 twice a day, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, pantoprazole; finished cipro yesterday. HCTZ stopped. Home weight down 3 kg since discharge. No confusion. Not drinking.

Exam: BP 112/70, HR in the 60s. Pale. Mild scleral icterus. Spider angiomata on the chest. Abdomen distended, soft, shifting dullness present, spleen tip palpable. Periumbilical venous pattern. Trace ankle edema. No asterixis.

A/P
1. Decompensated cirrhosis, HCV: BMP, CBC, hepatic panel, INR today. Continue spironolactone 100 / furosemide 40, 2 g sodium. Daily weights; call for gain over 1 kg a day or 2 kg a week, or dizziness.
2. Varices s/p banding: propranolol 20 BID; repeat EGD 7/30.
3. HTN: off HCTZ, BP fine on propranolol and diuretics.
4. Medication safety: no NSAIDs; acetaminophen max 2 g/day.
Med rec done. Back in 4 weeks.

Addendum 7/14: Na 135, K 4.3, creatinine 0.9; Hgb 9.3, platelets 86K; bilirubin 3.8, albumin 2.6, INR 1.6. Holding steady. Patient messaged.

documents.title: Your labs from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, Friday's results: sodium, potassium and kidney function are fine on the new water pills. Hemoglobin is 9.3, up a little from the hospital. Bilirubin 3.8 and INR 1.6 are a bit better than at admission. Keep going with the diet and the daily weights; see you August 8.

documents.title: RE: Your labs from Friday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Weight this morning 70.6. Is canned soup completely off the table?

documents.title: RE: Your labs from Friday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Most canned soups are very high in sodium, so yes, best avoided. Low-sodium versions can fit if you count them toward your 2,000 mg for the day. I'll send you the handout on reading labels.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology endoscopy unit
Date of procedure: 07/30/2025
Indication: esophageal varices, bled 07/02, follow-up band ligation.
Medications: propranolol 20 mg BID, spironolactone 100 mg, furosemide 40 mg, pantoprazole. NKDA.
Sedation: MAC.
Findings: persistent varices in the distal esophagus; post-banding ulcers healing. Four bands placed. Stomach and duodenum normal.
Impression: esophageal varices, banded x4.
Plan: repeat EGD with banding in 4 weeks. Pantoprazole course is complete; no need to continue. Continue propranolol.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cirrhosis f/u, 1 month out from the bleed.

Banded again 7/30 (x4), next 8/27. Belly noticeably smaller, ankles better. Weight 68 kg today, 74 at admission. Energy slowly improving; back at work part days. No black stools, no vomiting, no confusion. Following the 2 g sodium diet carefully.

Meds: propranolol 20 BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40. Pantoprazole finished.

Exam: BP and pulse as charted, pulse high 50s. Mild icterus. Abdomen soft, much less distended, mild shifting dullness. Trace edema at the ankles. No asterixis.

A/P
1. Cirrhosis with ascites: improving on diuretics. Labs today.
2. Varices: banding program per GI. Continue propranolol.
3. Anemia after the bleed: recovering, CBC today.

Addendum: Na 134, K 4.6, creatinine 1.0; Hgb 10.4, plt 89K; AST 88, ALT 60, bilirubin 2.9, albumin 2.8, INR 1.5. All moving the right way. No diuretic change. Recheck in about 3 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cirrhosis, 4 months after the bleed.

Back at work full time. Weight steady at 68-69 at home. Last banding 10/8, one more planned this month. No bleeding. Has a dry cough for about a month, no fever, no sputum, no shortness of breath.

Meds: propranolol 20 BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40. Had flu and COVID shots 10/6.

Exam: vitals as charted. Sclerae barely icteric. Lungs clear throughout, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, minimal fluid. No ankle edema. No asterixis.

A/P
1. Cirrhosis: labs today. Ascites well controlled on current doses.
2. Varices: eradication EGD this month.
3. Cough, about a month, lungs clear: watch for now; let me know if it lingers or changes.

Addendum: Hgb 11.6, plt 92K; bilirubin 1.9, albumin 3.2, INR 1.3; creatinine 0.9. Best numbers since July.

orders.reason: Right lower lobe lung mass with weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit. The cough from November never went away: now about 3 months, dry, worse at night. She has lost 10 lb without trying, 68.5 kg in November to 64 today. No fever, no night sweats, no hemoptysis. Never smoker.

Exam: afebrile, BP 130/85, RR 16, sat as charted. Decreased breath sounds over the right lower lobe posteriorly; no wheezes or crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no appreciable fluid. No edema.

CXR done here this morning: 2.5 cm mass at the periphery of the right lower lobe.

A/P
Right lower lobe mass with 3 months of cough and 10 lb weight loss in a never smoker with cirrhosis: needs CT and tissue promptly. Spoke with the on-call pulmonologist at the regional hospital, who will take her as a direct admission tomorrow for CT and biopsy, given the liver disease and low platelets. Pt agrees. She'll bring her medicine bottles and arrange a ride.
